gen-gf-lilex-fs-literata: Precise and technical, Lilex sets its fixed-width letters apart with wide gaps and a caliper-like c, while Literata keeps a gentle thick-thin rhythm. The text serif softens the code-style rigidity.
gen-gf-livvic-fs-literata: Livvic draws every letter at a uniform line width, quiet and level, while Literata, a serif, lets its thick strokes lean just slightly heavier than its thin ones. Make the heading small and that restraint nearly vanishes.
gen-gf-lunasima-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sturdy, its hairlines neither wispy nor heavy, and its curves open wide as if unlatched. Lunasima is best at friendly, horseshoe-open headings; the classic serif is best at carrying the words.
gen-gf-lustria-fs-bespoke-sans: Lustria's rounds stay unsealed, like an unlatched hook, with a faint thick-thin shift that feels traditional and editorial. It excels at announcing; Bespoke Sans, sharp and refined, excels at spacing out what follows.
gen-gf-lxgw-wenkai-mono-tc-fs-bespoke-sa: Brush-lifted curve ends make LXGW WenKai Mono TC feel hand-touched yet fixed in width. Bespoke Sans follows with generous gaps between curve ends and stems, giving the sharp, refined text room to breathe beneath it.
gen-gf-lxgw-wenkai-mono-tc-fs-literata: Literata reads sturdy and bookish, its thin and thick strokes only mildly different, like a brush barely pressed. And LXGW WenKai Mono TC contributes a glowing, single-thickness, fixed-width precision that the classic serif lacks.
gen-gf-m-plus-1-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sophisticated, with its middling contrast like a flat brush held half-turned, so each line feels warmly drawn. And its open curves keep the eye moving easily down the page beneath M PLUS 1.
gen-gf-m-plus-1p-fs-literata: Clean lines, lots of light: M PLUS 1p lets white space leak in freely, with low contrast and a professional finish. Literata, the text serif, holds steady across a long stretch, its strokes sitting between monoline and sharp.
gen-gf-m-plus-2-fs-literata: Neon-glass tubing is what M PLUS 2 resembles, each letter traced with one marker. Literata, a classic serif, adds joins that taper modestly, so the pairing mixes a smooth heading with a bookish, sturdy text.
gen-gf-m-plus-code-latin-fs-literata: Literata has sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones, like etched lines in glass. Its strongest quality is a bookish warmth that M PLUS Code Latin, poured at one flat width, sets off cleanly.
